Summary Description: Liu Hong's research lies at the intersection of medical imaging, radiomics, and computational optics. Across multiple papers, Liu develops AI-driven CAD and risk-stratification frameworks for breast cancer detection, leveraging bilateral mammographic symmetry, multi-feature neural fusion, and advanced transformer architectures to fuse information from multiple views. He also pursues data-efficient learning via semi-supervised methods (VAT) to maximize utility from limited labeled data. In addition, his work extends into computational imaging with Fourier Ptychographic Microscopy to achieve high-resolution, wide-field chromosome imaging for karyotyping, including phase and amplitude reconstructions and MTF-based performance benchmarks. Overall, his work aims to enable clinically feasible, robust, and scalable imaging analytics that augment radiology and cytogenetics, with careful attention to data handling, evaluation rigor, and potential translational impact.
